texts: On day 485 of Year 2, Tam Harrow missed the midnight check at his station on the Middle Row, because his child was ill.
Tam Harrow was a junior Keeper.
Tam Harrow returned to the station at the third watch.
The station was not at the Sunken Cove.
Tam Harrow reported the incident to the Council the next morning.

q1_issues.issue: The reified state sk_ill_1 for the past-tense "his child was ill" carries no (Past sk_ill_1) atom even though the flat half is Past-wrapped, unlike the instruction set's parallel reified-state pattern for "Alice was ill on Friday".

q2_gaps: Negative determiner on an episodic object NP ("The Council issued no penalty"): the instruction set covers "no/none" only as a subject quantifier on copular generics, rules and partitives, and its mandatory-QuantifierPhrase clause presupposes a quantified range that an ordinary strength-0 event denial does not have, so it never says whether object-position "no N" is a plain event denial, needs a companion, or needs a zero-count record.
review.notes: The instruction set is itself inconsistent about tensing a reified connective-endpoint state (the "wallpaper peeled because it was damp" example tenses neither half, the Time section's copular example tenses both), so the flagged omission is partly an instruction-set ambiguity. Resolving "the incident" to the missed-check event and the "burning low" adverbial to Manner are both judgment calls the instruction set leaves open but does not forbid; the wick correctly gets no invented PartOf to the lantern.

issues.reason: "his child was ill" is a finite past clause, and *Status predicates* puts tense on the eventuality it reifies — the Time section's parallel "Alice was ill on Friday" emits (Past sk_ill_1) beside the flat (Past (Member alice ill)) — so the untensed state witness reads as the unmarked/dispositional default ("an event with no status predicate is generic / habitual / dispositional"), asserting a standing illness the text does not state and contradicting the parse's own Past-wrapped flat half.

gaps_confirmed: Object-position negative determiner in an episodic clause ("issued no penalty"): the instruction set fixes the strength-0 event denial but leaves undecided whether the explicit quantifier word "no" takes a QuantifierPhrase companion, whose (subject predicate "word") slots presuppose a quantified range an episodic denial has not got.
new_gaps: Fictional day-of-year dating ("day 485 of Year 2"): (Day <n>) is the day-of-month slot, so a day-of-year value has no licensed term and is only carried by overloading that constructor (the "next morning" 485→486 increment inherits the same overload).

A flat degree/extent adverbial on a process verb ("the lantern was burning low"): *Adverbs that are not Manner* reserves Manner for manner proper and gives a verb-modifying degree adverb no slot at all, so the only licensed move is to drop the word — losing the very state that motivates the refill and the later "recovered".
adjudication.defect_summary: Emit (Past sk_ill_1) on the reified state witness alongside the existing (Member sk_ill_1 ill) / (Experiencer sk_ill_1 sk_child_1) and the flat (Past (Member sk_child_1 ill)), exactly as the "Alice was ill on Friday" pattern does; nothing else in the because-clause encoding changes.
adjudication.notes: The connectives section's own "because it was damp" illustration omits tense on both endpoints — including the indisputably required (Past sk_peel_1) — so it is abbreviated on tense rather than a licence to leave a reified past state unmarked. The "next morning" day-increment, the entity-attached (On sk_station_1 middle_row), the negated (Past (LocatedIn …)) and the absence of an invented wick/lantern PartOf are all correct.
